column1: # A night of three sittings, 8.6 wall hours, 7.9 broadcast hours, ~7.7 BZZ on the uploader.
# Columns are tab separated: name, deadline minutes, driver, settings.
# Read `overnight-chain.sh` for what stops this and `docs/bench/night-2026-08-12-prediction.md` for
# what each sitting is expected to find, registered before any of it was spent.
# ⭐ ORDER IS DELIBERATE. The short sitting goes first because it exercises the whole chain end to
# end for 56 broadcast minutes and 0.9 BZZ. If the gates, the publisher, the browser, the sampler or
# the teardown are broken, that is when it is found, not four hours into a soak.
# The two soaks then go longest-first, so the one that can absorb a late start is the one that runs
# last. A soak cut short is still a result: three hours beats every ten-minute run in the corpus.
# ⛔ 720p throughout. The burn constants in the drivers are 720p figures and 1080p costs about 2.2x.
# #91, and the only sitting here with a control arm. OBS ships a 2.0s GOP, so 2.0 is the GOP most
# likely to arrive uninvited, and everything known about it is inference. 2 arms x 4 rounds x 7 min,
# first round discarded, direction reversed each round.
obs-default-vs-shipped
# #89, the single biggest gap in the corpus: nothing here has ever run past ten minutes, and every
# claim about a longer broadcast is a projection from a synthetic fill. Four hours at the shipping
# profile reaches ~28,800 real segments. WARMUP_ROUNDS=0 because a soak has nothing to warm up for
# and labelling its only round as discarded would file four hours as a warm-up nobody counted.
long-broadcast-shipped
# #89 again at the GOP a broadcaster actually sends, which makes this a second question rather than a
# replicate: at 2.0s the segment peaks at 2.133s so TARGETDURATION is 3, and the stall penalty caps at
# 3.0s instead of 1.0s. Whether that ratchet bites over hours has never been watched.
long-broadcast-obs
